questions.stem: A nurse manager uses a servant-leadership approach. Which behavior best reflects this leadership style?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Centralizing authority so staff members have little opportunity to develop autonomy or leadership capacity.","B":"Prioritizing the leader's status and recognition when those goals conflict with the growth of team members.","C":"Avoiding difficult decisions so responsibility for team outcomes rests entirely with frontline staff.","D":"Supporting the growth, development, and needs of team members while remaining accountable for leadership decisions and outcomes."}}
questions.rationale: Servant leadership emphasizes serving and developing others, stewardship, listening, and enabling team members to grow. It does not mean avoiding accountability or refusing to make necessary leadership decisions.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Leadership and Management
questions.source_detail: Servant leadership emphasizes service to others, staff development, stewardship, and shared growth while maintaining leadership responsibility.

questions.stem: A new nurse reports repeated belittling comments, social exclusion, and intimidation from a colleague. How should the charge nurse interpret this behavior?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"As workplace bullying or lateral violence that should be addressed through organizational safety and reporting processes.","B":"As a normal socialization practice that new nurses should tolerate until they become established on the unit.","C":"As a private interpersonal issue with no recognized relationship to staff well-being, retention, or patient safety.","D":"As conduct that should be ignored unless physical injury occurs because verbal and relational aggression are not workplace-safety concerns."}}
questions.rationale: ANA identifies incivility, bullying, lateral violence, and workplace violence as serious organizational and professional concerns. Repeated belittling, intimidation, and exclusion should not be normalized as part of nursing socialization and should be addressed through established reporting and prevention processes.
questions.source_name: American Nurses Association — Workplace Violence Position Statement
questions.source_detail: ANA recognizes bullying, incivility, and lateral violence as threats to a respectful and safe nursing work environment and calls for organizational prevention, reporting, investigation, and response.

questions.stem: A nurse educator explains the difference between a preceptor and a mentor. Which description best fits a preceptor?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A clinician assigned to provide structured, role-specific orientation, supervision, feedback, and skill development for a defined period.","B":"A person whose only function is long-term informal career advice without responsibility for clinical orientation or competency development.","C":"A role that is interchangeable with mentoring because preceptorship has no defined educational or clinical purpose.","D":"A manager who performs formal disciplinary evaluation but does not support transition into a clinical role or practice setting."}}
questions.rationale: Preceptorship is generally a structured, time-limited clinical teaching relationship focused on transition into a specific role or practice setting, including supervision, feedback, and competency development. Mentoring is typically broader and may be longer-term and career focused.
questions.source_detail: Preceptors support structured clinical orientation, role transition, supervision, feedback, and development of clinical competence.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes continuous quality improvement in healthcare?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"It is an ongoing process of measuring performance, learning from results, testing changes, and improving systems rather than merely confirming minimum compliance.","B":"It is limited to determining whether a fixed standard was met and ends once the organization demonstrates compliance.","C":"It focuses primarily on assigning individual blame after an adverse event instead of improving the processes that shape performance.","D":"It is unrelated to routine clinical operations because quality improvement is performed only during external accreditation surveys."}}
questions.rationale: IHI describes quality improvement as a systematic, learning-oriented approach to improving performance and redesigning processes. Modern quality management integrates planning, control, and continuous improvement rather than relying only on reactive compliance checks.
questions.source_name: Institute for Healthcare Improvement — Whole System Quality
questions.source_detail: IHI describes quality improvement as part of a continuous learning system that integrates quality planning, quality control, and improvement activities.

questions.stem: A client with decision-making capacity says the current care plan does not reflect the client's goals. The nurse raises the concern during the interprofessional discussion. Which nursing role is demonstrated?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Patient advocacy, because the nurse is helping protect the client's rights, preferences, and informed participation in care.","B":"Boundary violation, because nurses should not communicate a capable client's expressed goals to other members of the healthcare team.","C":"Unauthorized prescribing, because discussing the client's goals is equivalent to independently changing the medical treatment plan.","D":"Case management only, because advocacy for a client's wishes is not part of professional nursing ethics or practice."}}
questions.rationale: Advocacy is a core nursing responsibility. ANA ethical guidance supports nurses in protecting patients' rights, promoting informed decision-making, and communicating patient preferences within the healthcare team.
questions.source_name: American Nurses Association — Code of Ethics for Nurses / Patient Advocacy
questions.source_detail: ANA ethical standards identify advocacy for patient health, safety, rights, preferences, and informed decision-making as a professional nursing responsibility.

questions.stem: A client with decision-making capacity refuses a recommended treatment after receiving information about the proposed treatment, expected benefits, material risks, and alternatives. What should the nurse do?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Respect the refusal, document the relevant education and the client's decision according to policy, and communicate the refusal to the appropriate clinician or team.","B":"Document only the words 'client refused' because information provided before the refusal has no relevance to the clinical record.","C":"Proceed with the treatment because a capable patient's refusal becomes invalid whenever clinicians believe the treatment is beneficial.","D":"Ask a family member to override the client's decision because informed refusal applies only when the healthcare team agrees with the patient's choice."}}
questions.rationale: A patient with decision-making capacity has the right to withhold informed consent. Safe practice includes respecting the decision, documenting the refusal and relevant information provided according to organizational policy, and communicating the decision to the responsible clinical team. The original item was narrowed to avoid claiming a single universal documentation formula for every jurisdiction and setting.
questions.source_name: The Joint Commission — National Performance Goal: Safe Informed Care
questions.source_detail: Joint Commission patient-rights standards require respect for the patient's right to give or withhold informed consent and communication in a manner the patient can understand.

questions.stem: A client with asthma asks which exposures can trigger symptoms. Which response is accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Triggers can include respiratory viral infections, tobacco smoke, cold air, exercise, and relevant allergens, although individual triggers vary.","B":"Food exposure is the only recognized trigger category, so environmental and respiratory exposures do not need to be considered.","C":"Exercise is the only predictable trigger, and viral infections, smoke, allergens, and weather changes do not affect asthma symptoms.","D":"Asthma symptoms occur independently of identifiable exposures, so identifying and reducing individual triggers is not useful."}}
questions.rationale: GINA identifies multiple common asthma triggers, including viral respiratory infections, tobacco smoke, cold air or weather changes, exercise, and allergens in susceptible individuals. Trigger profiles vary, so teaching should be individualized rather than implying every patient reacts to every exposure.
questions.source_name: Global Initiative for Asthma — Asthma Triggers
questions.source_detail: GINA identifies cold air, viral respiratory infection, tobacco smoke, exercise, and allergens among common triggers, with individual variation.

questions.stem: Which finding is classically associated with the chronic bronchitis phenotype of COPD rather than emphysema?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Chronic cough with sputum production; the traditional epidemiologic definition is cough and sputum for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years.","B":"Destruction of alveolar walls and enlargement of distal air spaces as the defining pathologic abnormality of the chronic bronchitis phenotype.","C":"Absence of cough and sputum because mucus hypersecretion is not associated with chronic bronchitis in patients with COPD.","D":"A disease pattern unrelated to tobacco exposure or other inhaled irritants, because airway inflammation is not involved in chronic bronchitis."}}
questions.rationale: Chronic bronchitis is classically defined epidemiologically by chronic cough and sputum production for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years after excluding other causes. Emphysema instead refers to destructive enlargement of distal air spaces. The two phenotypes can overlap in COPD.
questions.source_name: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease — GOLD Report
questions.source_detail: GOLD distinguishes chronic bronchitis symptoms from emphysema pathology and recognizes the traditional chronic bronchitis definition while noting phenotype overlap in COPD.

questions.stem: A client develops reproducible calf discomfort while walking that resolves after several minutes of rest. What does this pattern most strongly suggest?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Intermittent claudication associated with lower-extremity peripheral artery disease and impaired blood flow during exertion.","B":"A normal consequence of aging that does not warrant vascular assessment when the pain consistently resolves with rest.","C":"Deep vein thrombosis, which is characteristically defined by reproducible exertional pain that disappears promptly with rest.","D":"Restless legs syndrome, which typically produces the same predictable exertional ischemic pain pattern during walking."}}
questions.rationale: The AHA describes intermittent claudication as lower-extremity discomfort provoked by walking or exercise and relieved by rest. This is a classic symptom of peripheral artery disease and should not be dismissed as normal aging.
questions.source_name: American Heart Association — Symptoms of Peripheral Artery Disease
questions.source_detail: AHA describes intermittent claudication as leg discomfort during activity that improves after stopping and resting.

questions.stem: A client has chronic lower-leg swelling, aching and heaviness, varicose veins, and skin changes that become more noticeable after prolonged standing and improve with leg elevation. Which condition best matches this pattern?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Chronic venous insufficiency caused by impaired venous return and venous hypertension in the lower extremities.","B":"Lower-extremity arterial insufficiency, whose classic exertional ischemic pattern is better characterized by claudication relieved by rest.","C":"An uncomplicated musculoskeletal disorder, because edema, varicosities, and stasis-related skin changes do not indicate venous disease.","D":"A normal age-related finding that requires no vascular assessment even when progressive edema and skin changes are present."}}
questions.rationale: The Society for Vascular Surgery describes chronic venous insufficiency as impaired venous return with symptoms such as leg or ankle swelling, aching or heaviness, varicose veins, and skin changes. Symptoms often worsen with prolonged standing and may improve with elevation or compression. This pattern differs from classic arterial claudication.
questions.source_name: Society for Vascular Surgery — Chronic Venous Insufficiency
questions.source_detail: CVI commonly causes swelling, heaviness, discomfort, varicose veins and skin changes; prolonged standing worsens symptoms and leg elevation can provide relief.
